title: Charge polarity determination
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly identify the particle's charge as negative, based on the direction of its acceleration relative to the electric field.

title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must calculate the correct magnitude of the electric field strength, approximately 462 V/m or 800√3/3 V/m.

title: Charge-to-mass ratio
description: Essential Criteria: The student must calculate the correct charge-to-mass ratio, 1.875 × 10¹⁰ C/kg.

title: Potential at key points
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly determine the potentials at points A and F using the given potentials and the uniform field property (e.g., φ_B - φ_C = φ_F - φ_E).

title: Geometry and displacement
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the displacement AE (≈0.173 m) using the hexagon's geometry and recognize it as the relevant distance for the potential difference.

title: Kinematic application
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly apply kinematics, using the time of flight from A to D and the displacement AE to relate acceleration to q/m.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student makes a sign error in potential differences, incorrectly assigns charge polarity, or misapplies the direction of acceleration.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The student's work demonstrates consistent use of SI units and correct unit analysis throughout the calculation.
